file_conventions: Applies to every entry in this file. Research date 2026-11-10. verified=true means a supplier, manufacturer or parts-library page for that exact part was fetched and showed it listed for sale or in the library; stock_note says what the page actually showed. 'read' means read from the PDF itself. 'search snippet', 'from memory' and 'my calculation / inference' mean NOT seen on a fetched product page. JLCPCB and LCSC pages did not expose live stock or price to a page fetch, so JLCPCB entries confirm library membership and class only. PLN converted at an assumed 0.27 USD/PLN.
note: Model check (my calculation, assuming the datasheet '10 V' is 10 Vrms sine and a square wave's fundamental is 4/pi of half its swing): the generic part's guaranteed 110 dB corresponds to about 0.12 Pa*m per Vpp of square drive, below the 0.17 used in replicator/constants.py (P_REF_PER_VPP); Manorshi's claimed 115 dB gives about 0.21; Murata nominal 120 dB gives about 0.38. So the cheapest part may deliver about 3 dB less pressure than the simulation assumes unless units are measured or sorted. Murata's 20 Vp-p is an absolute maximum, so 18 V drive leaves 10 %. Murata at ~$4.28 for 475 pieces is about $2,030.
